question: Can teacher talk moves be classified across transcripts?
data: TalkMoves: 175,129 teacher utterances; 565 content-defined transcript groups.
method: Remove exact text-label transcript duplicates; group by ordered text hash; compare majority and TF-IDF logistic baselines on transcript-held-out data.
interpretation: Exact text-label duplicate transcripts are removed. Transcripts with identical ordered text share a split group even if annotations differ. This prevents identical copies from crossing partitions, but does not establish teacher-, school- or near-duplicate-disjoint evaluation. One split and one model configuration limit generalization.
evidence_note: GitHub Actions run 36250532574; seed 42; macro-F1 is the primary metric.
finding: This TalkMoves study compares a majority baseline with TF-IDF logistic regression for teacher talk-move classification. The completed run removes duplicate transcript copies and groups matching transcript text before splitting, yielding 565 content-defined transcript groups and 175,129 labeled teacher utterances. On 113 held-out groups, logistic regression achieves macro-F1 0.5198 versus 0.1152 for the majority baseline, while accuracy remains similar. These results concern coded discourse moves, not teaching quality.
